spite remarkable progress in visual fidelity, existing T2V           viate sharply from physical reality as Figure 1 shows.
approaches remain predominantly appearance-driven rather                 A parallel limitation arises in evaluation methodology.

motion, dynamics, and causality, revealing a critical gap            Fréchet video distance (FVD) [41] to assess performance.

                                                                 2
Figure 2. Overview of our multi-agent motion-reasoning engine (MoReGen) for physics-grounded text-to-video synthesis. MoReGen focuses on achieving
high-precision Newtonian motion through coordinated multi-agent reasoning. Given a natural language prompt, the text-parser agent Atext extracts physical
parameters and motion descriptors, which are then translated into executable simulation code by the code-writer agent Acoder . The resulting code is
executed within a sandboxed video-render agent Arender to produce a physically plausible video. This video serves as the basis for evaluator feedback,
guiding enhancements in code robustness and physical fidelity for subsequent iterations. By leveraging open-source LLMs, few-shot tuning of Atext and
multi-modal evaluator, MoReGen enables accurate and reproducible Newtonian motion synthesis from natural language instructions.

precise T2V generation by explicitly modeling Newtonian                   We adopt SFT to enable Atext to internalize the mapping
motion through multi-agent collaboration. Given a natu-               from natural language to structured physics specifications,

an evaluator: a text-parser agent Atext , a code-writer agent         tion suffices to generate complete and physically consistent
Acoder , a video-render agent Arender and multi-component             specifications across all phenomena. During training, the
evaluator E (see Figure 2). All three agents are LLM-                 model learns lightweight linguistic reasoning rules (e.g., in-
based (Qwen in our case). As illustrated in Algorithm 1,              terpreting “first two balls” or “pushed from the right” into

nian specification, and Acoder converts this specification into       ity to infer missing parameters while avoiding hallucinated

trajectories. Arender then produces a rendering script that           1 × 10−5 ) for five epochs. The model is optimized with

                                                                                  4.2. Evaluation Metrics
                                                                                  Existing physics-aware metrics remain inadequate for as-
                                                                                  sessing physical validity, as they emphasize perceptual sim-
                                                                                  ilarity or in-distribution priors over causal motion accuracy.
                                                                                  MoRe Metrics. Instead of pixel-level similarity metrics
                                                                                  (FID, FVD, PSNR, and LPIPS) or latent-space features
                                                                                  from pretrained video encoders (Trajan, VideoPhy), we pro-
                                                                                  pose MoRe metrics, a trajectory-based suite comprised of
                                                                                  dynamic time warping (DTW), Normalized DTW (DTW-
                                                                                  N) and Procrustes Analysis. These metrics directly mea-
Figure 3. Sample frames and corresponding text prompts from our MoRe-

corresponds to the rightmost video in the second row, with highlighted text       detection, and tracks its trajectory throughout the video. We
emphasizing the numerical relationships depicted in the scene.
                                                                                  then compute: (1) DTW [39] to align estimated trajectories
                                                                                  with ground-truth sequences of varying temporal lengths
fying the physical validity of generated videos beyond vi-                        by projecting them into a non-linear space; (2) DTW-N to
sual realism. We demonstrate that existing benchmarks and                         normalize distance across clips of different scales and du-
metrics fail to capture fundamental Newtonian principles                          rations; and (3) Procrustes Analysis Score [15] to assess

Figure 4. Qualitative comparison of our model with recent open-source and commercial models, prompted to generate a video of Newton’s cradle. We used
the same prompt across the board: “Generate a video that showcase the following scene: Five shiny metal balls of a newton’s cradle is visible, along with
parts of a single vertical string for each metal ball respectively. These strings keeps their respective metal ball suspended. The top part of the newton’s cradle
is not visible. The camera faces all the five metal balls. The first and leftmost ball is at an angle of 30 degrees from the cradle and released. Due to gravity,
the ball comes and strikes the second ball from the left. This causes momentum to be transferred to the fifth and the right most ball which is launched at
a slightly lesser angle, having lost some momentum. This process keeps repeating itself till the rightmost ball has lost a lot of momentum when the video
ends.” For Grok Imagine, we always select the first video; for WISA, we use Qwen3-4B to generate asset .json file from our prompt.

evaluation set from our dataset, with tests performed on Qwen2.5 Coder and GPT-5. Feedback involves one iteration of processing the video to extract object
trajectories, comparing them with ground truth, and obtaining an overall evaluation from Qwen2.5-VL. GPT-5 then summarizes this evaluation into a list of
actionable improvements, which are fed into the Coder Agent. If the code contains syntax error, GPT-5 is asked to correct the issue without providing the
